name: Ui_Prop_SpawnChildEffects
summary: Creates the two child effect instances a UI prop owns: it takes the prop's child-bounds centre, spawns the effect id stored in the prop's first two u16 fields and keeps the handles at +0x1DA/+0x1DC, playing each slot's sound effect.
evidence: Confident neighbours fix the family: the caller is Battle_Ui_UpdateStateMachine and the callees are Ui_Prop_CalcChildBoundsCenter, Ui_LayoutParams_Init and Effect_FindOrCreateInstance, all UI code - so the old Field_Prop prefix was wrong. Sound_PlaySeById confirms the per-slot SE.

name: maybe_Ui_Prop_UpdateChildEffects
summary: Per-frame sibling of 0x004E3714: re-creates the prop's child effect when the slot id changes, walks the child model slots, applies the layout parameters and plays the slot SE.
evidence: It shares all five confident callees with 0x004E3714 (Ui_Prop_CalcChildBoundsCenter, Effect_FindOrCreateInstance, Ui_LayoutParams_Init, Sound_GetPlayer, Sound_PlaySeById) and the same handle-table validity checks, which moves it into the Ui_Prop family; it still has no caller, so which state drives it is unknown.

name: Model_GetNamedNodeWorldPosition
summary: Writes the world position of a named model node: starts from the zero vector, finds the node id by name, applies its transform and adds the model offset from the 0x7E7110 table.
evidence: The callee set is now Model_GetNodeIdByName plus Game_GetDataManager, and the only caller is the confident Ui_Prop_CalcChildBoundsCenter - exactly the position-of-this-named-child-node use the name claims. The trailing out[1] = 0 store looks like decompiler dead-store noise.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_StartMultiVoiceNote
signature: u32 maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_StartMultiVoiceNote(void *player, int restart, u32 *outSlots, u32 expectedId)
summary: Starts a sequence note that fans out to up to eight voices: allocates the voice slots from the mixer, starts them with priority 0x7FFF, queues one stream read per slot and then arms the per-channel output mode and loop flags.
evidence: Caller Sound_Command_ExecuteList (the sequence-command dispatcher) and the confident voice callees Sound_Voice_StartVoiceChannels, Sound_Voice_CalculatePitch, Sound_Voice_Stop and Sound_Track_CheckDuration confirm the sequencer role and the multi-voice fan-out (loop bound player[0x2D] clamped to 8, one voice slot per iteration, then the per-channel output-mode/loop-flag pass). The voice priority itself is read from unaff_r7 (=0x7FFF), so the allocation detail is damaged in the readable C and the name stays maybe_.

name: Ui_TextColor_Resolve
summary: Resolves the text colour of a character id: reads the record through func_0035EB98, unpacks the RGB565-style u16 at +0x14 plus the record's virtual slot +8 and writes the packed colour to *out.
evidence: Five confident callers - Ui_ApplyTextColor, Ui_ApplyTextColorAlt, Ui_StatusPanel_SetCharacter, Ui_StatusPanel_SetCharacterField and Ui_PartySelectWindow_RefreshRows - all use it as a per-character colour lookup, which is what the name says. func_0035EB98 is the engine's party-record accessor, so the argument really is a character/member id rather than a generic style id.

name: Text_Command26_SpawnActorPopup
signature: void Text_Command26_SpawnActorPopup(void *screen, u32 arg2, void *actor, u32 isLast)
summary: Inline text command 0x26: plays the acting member's sound effect, sets the actor's pose and spawns the emote popup anchored on that actor, falling back to the generic row-popup path.
evidence: The caller is now the text-script walker Text_Layout_StepLine and the callees are Sound_PlaySeById, Text_Popup_SelectMessage, Text_QueueEffectCommand and Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFromTable - the popup path the header describes. The command id 0x26 is compared at dispatch site 0x4E05F4.

name: Field_Actor_CreateAttachedEffectParts
signature: void Field_Actor_CreateAttachedEffectParts(void *self, int variant, int tableId, float *rect, int style)
summary: Builds the two attached-effect parts of a field actor or gimmick: allocates a 0x220-byte effect part (direction, 0x78 width, 200 height) and a 0x250-byte one, initialises each through Field_Actor_InitAttachedEffect with the row/table id and places them on the target rectangle, rotated for the variant.
evidence: The callees now include the confident Field_Actor_InitAttachedEffect (0x0032D9B8), Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection and Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId, and the confident callers Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId and Field_Gimmick_UpdateRowStates are gimmick code. Nothing in the body allocates a UI window or fills a window descriptor, so the old Ui_Window_BuildDescriptor was misleading.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowAndStoreArgs
summary: Places one gimmick list row at the owner actor's position plus an offset scaled from args[0], re-applies the row's asset id (args[6]) and copies the 0x11-byte argument block into the state record at +0x1A8..+0x1C0 before signalling the state machine through the handle ref.
evidence: The confident callees are Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId and std_memcpy; the placement helper 0x005D2A00 is still unnamed and the function has no callers, so PlaceRow remains an inference from the position arithmetic rather than a named call.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowAndStoreArgsB
summary: Variant of 0x005E3FE0 that first clears the side-state flags (+0x23B0..+0x23B2 and the owner actor's +0x1464), then places the row and copies the same 0x11-byte argument block into the state record at +0x10EC/+0x1100.
evidence: Same two confident callees as 0x005E3FE0 (Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId, std_memcpy) and the same placement sequence; no caller was found and the write layout differs (two overlapping records), so the variant's purpose is still unproven.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetFromArgs
summary: Three-statement wrapper: resolves the owner actor through f_154C and forwards *args to Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId for row 0. The float conversion of args[1] and the resolved actor are both discarded in the readable C.
evidence: The body only calls the confident Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId; Ghidra kept the VectorSignedToFloat result in no variable and dropped the 0x4A1E00 return, so the from-args wording is accurate only for the id. Kept as maybe because two of the three arguments do nothing in the reconstruction.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlaceRowsAndStoreArgs
summary: Places two gimmick rows (asset ids args[5] at index 1 and args[2] at index -1) at the owner actor's current position, stores the actor/handle pair at +0x2DC/+0x2E0 and signals the handle-linked state machine.
evidence: Two confident Field_Gimmick_SetRowAssetId calls with the actor position from 0x4A1E00; there are no callers and no other confident callee, so PlaceRows is supported by the asset-id calls but the stored +0x2D4 value is still unexplained.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdateRotatingParts
summary: Re-creates the per-part effects of an animated gimmick: releases the old effect slots, builds each part's quaternion rotation from f_8C..f_98, spawns a scaled instance (effect 0x450) at the part position, plays the descriptor SEs and hands a component description to the UI hook.
evidence: Confident callees Field_Gimmick_ReleaseEffectSlots, Effect_CreateScaledInstance, Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and Ui_GetCore match the effect/part role; the quaternion algebra is unambiguous, so RotatingParts is supported even though the function also spawns the effects.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_AssignPartsAndTint
summary: Releases the effect slots, writes one tint/alpha byte into the six per-part colour fields and +0x1C8/+0x1CC, then rebuilds the part list by matching the configured part ids against the actor group's members and copies the 6-byte per-part records into both target objects.
evidence: Only one confident callee (Field_Gimmick_ReleaseEffectSlots) and the readable body reads its tint argument from unaff_r5, i.e. the register is lost; the two-pass match loop is visible but the 4th argument and the part-record semantics remain guesses.

name: Field_Gimmick_ReleaseEffectsAndModel
summary: Releases every effect slot of the gimmick (0x005DB018 with flag 0) and then asks the model object at +0x90 to finish through its vtable slot +0x14.
evidence: The body is two calls: the confident Field_Gimmick_ReleaseEffectSlots and a vtable +0x14 finish call on f_90; both halves are directly visible, so the descriptive name is safe.

name: Casino_IsJackpotClockExpired
summary: Returns true when any of the four stored jackpot timestamps (work+0x24A98 plus 0x31FC/0x3204/0x320C/0x3214) lies outside the current clock window, i.e. the cached jackpot state is stale.
evidence: All ten callers are the confident jackpot accessors (Casino_GetJackpotState, Casino_GetJackpotCoinNum, Casino_GetJackpotCoinStage, Casino_GetJackpotBunnyCoin, Casino_RollJackpotChance and friends), exactly the revalidate-the-cached-jackpot-before-reading role the name describes.

name: BattleScene_LayoutUnitModel
signature: u32 BattleScene_LayoutUnitModel(void *scene, void *unit, u32 pos, int offset)
summary: Places one battle unit's model on screen: picks the model track, resolves the unit's height and variant from the model table, writes the slide position and registers the keyframe track; returns 1 when a model was laid out.
evidence: Confident callees Event_ActorModels_AddModel, Event_ActorModels_AllocModelSlot, Event_ActorModels_LoadPartResources, Anim_TimeTrack_SetKeyframe and Pack_ReleaseHandle show the model-slot plus keyframe path the name claims; no caller was found, so it is a vtable/action callback.

name: maybe_BattleScene_ResolveModelRecord
summary: Resolves a battle model record and its variant for a model id through the battle model tables; the result is used through the returned record rather than returned by value.
evidence: The first pass guessed ResolveModelSize, but the confident callers (BattleScene_BuildPartyModel, BattleScene_PositionUnitModelWithAnim, BattleScene_ValidateModelForUnit, BattleScene_UpdateScreenState0Main) and the confident callee BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant show it resolves a model record/variant - no size value is ever computed or returned.

name: BattleScene_BuildUnitModelForAction
summary: Builds the battle model used by one member for an action: special-cases body id 0x360 (a guest/boss form) and otherwise reuses the party/member model builder and places the result in the requested slot.
evidence: Confident callees BattleScene_BuildMemberModel, BattleScene_BuildPartyModel and Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection match the build-a-unit-model-for-this-action role; the 0x360 special case is visible in the body and no caller exists because it is an action callback.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_UpdateEffectAnchors
summary: Recomputes the world anchor points a battle unit's state/action effects attach to, from the unit's grid position, facing and the field scene camera/map-rect helpers.
evidence: The old RefreshUnitStats wording is unsupported: the callers are Battle_SetupUnitFromMonsterData and the BattleActor_Show*Effect functions, and the callees are Field_SceneNode_GetPosition, Math_QuatToForwardVector, Field_Scene_GetCameraMode and Field_GetMapScreenSize - 3D anchor math, not stats.

name: maybe_Ui_Plate_FormatFullDescriptor
summary: Formats the full UTF-16 description/title text shown on a UI plate: it resolves the item or spell name through Ui_Message_GetItemDescription / Ui_Message_GetSpellDescription and copies it into the plate's text buffer.
evidence: Callers Ui_SkillPanel_ApplyState and Ui_SkillPanel_UpdateSkillDescription plus callees Ui_Message_GetItemDescription, Ui_Message_GetSpellDescription and std_wcsncpy confirm the format-the-detail-text role; Plate still comes from the caller's naming, since the function itself carries no pane name.

name: Sound_SeqParam_GetPointer
signature: u32 Sound_SeqParam_GetPointer(void *self, u32 id, u32 flags)
summary: Resolves a sequence parameter through the base sequence object unless an attached extension claims it: when the extension's flag byte +4 is set and its vtable slot +0x0C returns non-zero, the base lookup is skipped.
evidence: Five confident sound callers (Sound_Voice_SetupDspParameters, Sound_Voice_AllocateAndStart, Sound_ArchiveStream_StartStream, Sound_Voice_ConfigureDspChannels, Sound_Voice_ReleaseEntryStream) and the confident callee Sound_Seq_ResolveRecord confirm the parameter-resolution role; Ghidra dropped the return value, which is why the readable C says void.

name: Battle_ProcessUnitActions
summary: Per-unit action pass for the ally-side unit list: for each live, non-suppressed unit it resolves the data id, dispatches the pending action (or the fallback action with the unit's category) and decrements the unit's remaining-action counter.
evidence: The only caller is the confident Battle_Update, and the callees now include Ui_Widget_CountChildren and Ui_TextLayout_IsTypeAccepted, i.e. the tick also runs the queue widgets; the unit-list walk (+0x5C to +0x4254) and the counter decrement are visible in the body.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipPanel_UpdateCompareArrows
summary: Cheap per-frame poll of the equipment panel: compares the cached 12-byte equipment block with the previous copy, and when it changed re-targets the comparison panes and stores the new compare code; otherwise it only decrements the refresh delay.
evidence: No caller and no vtable slot were found, so dispatch is from a runtime table; the confident callees Item_LookupRecord, Model_Equip_ApplyAccessoryEffects and Text_GetCharPairStyle place it in equipment UI, but the arrows half is still inferred from which pane ids it writes.

name: maybe_Party_GetMaxMemberTimer
summary: Walks the active field-party actors and returns the largest u32 at +0xD8 of their party-member records (or 0 when none qualifies); the caller compares that value against an action start time.
evidence: Confident callees Menu_CountPartyActors and Menu_GetActorByIndex keep the walk honest, but the only caller is itself maybe_ (0x6374F4) and nothing in the body names the +0xD8 field, so Timer remains an inference.

name: maybe_Ui_SpawnEventBalloon
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_SpawnEventBalloon(void *self, int *event, int argument, u32 argument2)
summary: Spawns the balloon that belongs to a UI/field event record, choosing the balloon type from the event id through the 0x7B-offset table and finally queueing it with Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFromTable.
evidence: The Battle prefix is unsupported: the callers are field-party code (maybe_FieldParty_AdvanceMemberCursor, maybe_FieldParty_MemberAction_SpawnEventBalloon) plus Text_Window_UpdateAdvanceState, and the confident callees Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty and Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFromTable say queue a balloon for this actor. Kept as maybe because the caller names are themselves low-confidence.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_OpenCommandList
summary: Opens the battle command-list page: advances the window script to step 0x18, sets the command pane's page to 8 and applies the selected member id and command group.
evidence: The callees are now the confident Battle_CommandListWindow_BuildEntries and Battle_CommandListWindow_SelectEntryById, and the window-script call (vtable +0x4C, step 0x18) matches the other battle-window page openers.

name: Field_Action_UpdateMove
summary: Per-frame movement update of the field action: reads the analogue stick with the dead zone, integrates the delta, applies the move, and on a blocked move switches the action to the blocked state (or plays the bump reaction).
evidence: The callees Field_Action_ApplyMove, Input_ReadMoveStick3D and Input_ReadLookStick3D are now confident, which pins the analogue-move role; the blocked-move branch sets the actor's +0x276/+0x278/+0x27C values and calls the bump helper.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_ShowMessage17
summary: Shows a fixed battle message and advances the window script: it calls Ui_BattlePopup_Show with message 0x8C2, moves the script to step 0x11 and releases the auxiliary message window.
evidence: All three callees are confident (Ui_BattlePopup_Show, Ui_MessageWindow_ProcessCommands, Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseLayout), but 17 mixes the script step 0x11 with the message id and the function has no caller, so the exact meaning of the number stays unclear.

name: maybe_Ui_DungeonPlaceWindow_CreateBase
summary: Small constructor wrapper that builds the base object of a place/dungeon window and initialises its animation reference list.
evidence: Only two confident callees (Ui_Object_CtorBase, Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor) and no caller or vtable slot; the recovered header has no evidence section, so the DungeonPlaceWindow class name is still unproven.

name: Monster_ModelInstance_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a monster model instance: runs the whole base chain (transform, skeleton, colour block), sets twelve id/payload slots to -1/0 and clears two 0x60-byte vertex/colour buffers.
evidence: The caller Field_ObjectFactory_MonsterModel is now a confident name, exactly the factory that would construct a monster model instance; the base-ctor chain and the two 0x60-byte buffer clears are visible in the body.

name: maybe_Ui_HandleSet_DtorLarge
summary: Destructor of a medium UI object: releases the handle set at +0x84, stamps three sub-type words and returns this-0x84.
evidence: The only confident callee is Pack_ReleaseHandle; the object layout (this-0x84 return, three stamps) is visible, but which UI class this is has no support beyond the guessed prefix.

name: Sound_Driver_ShutdownHooks
summary: Final driver-shutdown step: stops the periodic timer, walks the second deferred list calling the finalise slot on each node and marks the driver closed (+0x1CC = -1).
evidence: The caller is the confident Sound_System_Shutdown, so this is a step of the sound-system teardown; the timer block at +0x1F4/+0x1F7 and the list walk are shared with the neighbouring shutdown function 0x0054DF34.

name: Field_Action_Run_CheckCanContinue
summary: Continuation test of the run action: returns -1 while the actor must keep moving, 3 when it may still run, and 1 when the run should end (both move bits clear, or no input while no auto-move distance is left).
evidence: It sits in slot 13 (offset 0x34) of the run-action vtable 0x00762B00 next to the confident Field_Action_UpdateMove, and its twin 0x00303858 occupies the same slot in the horse vtables - that slot pairing is the new evidence for the name.

name: Field_Action_Horse_CheckCanContinue
summary: Continuation test shared by the two horse actions: returns 2 while the rider is steering/accelerating, 3 when the actor may run on, and -1 when the action is finished.
evidence: It appears as slot 13 (offset 0x34) of both horse vtables 0x00762ABC and 0x00762B78, the same slot 0x0030271C fills for the run action; the return values 2/3/-1 are directly visible.

name: maybe_Svc_Ipc_CreateObjectFromBlock
signature: int maybe_Svc_Ipc_CreateObjectFromBlock(u32 *out, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 size, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8, u32 arg9, u32 arg10)
summary: Thin wrapper that builds a service/IPC object from a short argument block (0x00505058), writes a -1 handle next to the result and returns it.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Svc_Content_OpenByRecord and the only callee maybe_Svc_Object_CreateFromDescriptor, both low-confidence, so neither the IPC nor the from-block wording was confirmed by a named neighbour.

name: maybe_Ui_List_GetScrollRowIndex
summary: Turns the list's current scroll state into an absolute row index: takes the table size, adds the current row times the 5-unit row stride and subtracts the viewport base before resolving it through the row accessors; returns 0xFFFFFFFF when there is no row array.
evidence: The first pass called it HitTestRow, but the body takes no cursor position at all - it computes tableSize + row*5 - viewportBase and never tests a point, so the hit-test wording was wrong. Only one low-confidence caller remains, so the new scroll-index name stays maybe_.

name: Ui_TitleMessage_CreateChild
signature: void *Ui_TitleMessage_CreateChild(void *slot, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates the child title-message object for a handle slot: allocates the class-sized block, runs the title-message constructor, registers the object with the UI manager and activates its first page.
evidence: The callee Ui_TitleMessageWindow_Ctor is now confident (and called twice in the body) and Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable / Mem_AllocAligned_2 match the create-a-child-window pattern; the caller Gfx_Resource_Recreate34 only supplies the slot.

name: Ui_DualWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a holder with two owned windows: installs vtable 0x00762CD8, allocates and attaches the big 0x3DF4-byte window and the small 0x124-byte one, then starts and enables both.
evidence: The callees Ui_MemoriesWindow_Ctor and Ui_MemoriesWindow_CtorBase are now confident, so the two children are memories windows; the two allocate-ctor-attach-start sequences with sizes 0x3DF4/0x124 are visible, which is what DualWindow describes.

name: maybe_Ui_WindowHolder_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a tiny holder object (vtable 0x00760004): clears its two members, allocates a 0x3E0-byte child window, attaches it to the UI manager, configures it and starts it.
evidence: The ctor pattern is clear and Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable / Mem_AllocAligned_2 are confident, but the child ctor is still a maybe_ name (0x00304DCC) and the holder class itself carries no string, so the WindowHolder wording is unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_ScreenBase_Create
signature: void *maybe_Ui_ScreenBase_Create(void *owner, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Allocates a 0x328-byte screen object from the UI heap, constructs it with 0x1772C4 and either registers it with the screen manager or destroys it when registration is refused.
evidence: Ui_GetCore and Mem_AllocAligned_2 are confident, but the constructor 0x1772C4 is still maybe_Field_CreateScreenSystem, so whether this is a generic screen base or a specific screen cannot be settled from names yet; no caller was found (vtable slot).

name: maybe_Ui_DiveFormEx_Ctor
signature: void maybe_Ui_DiveFormEx_Ctor(u32 object, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Constructor variant of the dive-form window hierarchy: calls the confident Ui_DiveForm_Ctor, initialises the member pair and constructs the state-sequence array; the extra Ex suffix only distinguishes it from the other ctor variants.
evidence: Ui_DiveForm_Ctor and Ui_Object_InitMemberPair are confident callees and the cluster contains Ui_DiveForm_DerivedCtor / Ui_DiveForm_DeletingDestructor, which fixes the class family; the specific role of this variant (and therefore the Ex wording) is not recoverable from the body.

name: Field_SceneObject_ApplyVariantState
summary: Model-state update in vtable slot 10 of 0x778344: looks up the two ids at +0x2EC/+0x2EE, hides one set of model attach slots and shows the other, releases the stale effect handle and starts effect 0x4AC at the object position, then recomputes the alpha fade step.
evidence: Confident callees Model_AttachSlot_HideAll, Model_AttachSlot_ShowAll, Effect_ReleaseHandle and Effect_FindOrCreateInstance match the per-variant model/effect switch; the vtable slot and the f_2FC handle validation are visible in the body.

name: Field_SceneObject_OnEvent
signature: void Field_SceneObject_OnEvent(void *self, int eventId, u32 arg3)
summary: Event handler in vtable slot 12 of the scene-object vtable: event 0x10 runs the variant reset, then the event is forwarded to the node's children and to the attached object's virtual +0x38.
evidence: The callee Field_SceneNode_ForwardCommandToChildren is now confident and does exactly the child fan-out the body shows, and the 0x10 branch calls the variant-reset function 0x004C9D08 - the event-handler reading is confirmed.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_BeginMeshLoad
summary: Virtual slot 2 of the scene-node vtable 0x00778344, the hook between Gfx_SceneNode_LoadMeshByName (slot 1) and Gfx_Node_StopIfIdle (slot 3); the body itself is a stack-fixup fragment, so only the slot role is known.
evidence: No callees and no callers could be recovered, and the readable C is still a bad-data fragment containing unaff_ registers; the name records the vtable slot position only.

name: Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry
signature: int Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry(void *self, void *entry, u32 slot, u32 flags, int arg5)
summary: Commits one icon-cache entry: takes the monitor lock, resolves the entry's timestamp, writes the entry record and its page through the service helpers, then unlocks and notifies the waiting worker.
evidence: The caller Ui_IconCache_CommitEntryThunk is now confident and the callees include the confident Os_LockMonitor, Field_Clock_ConvertTimestamp and std_String_InitEmpty; the surrounding cluster is a fully named icon-cache service (RequestIcon, FetchIcon, ReadEntryTable).

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_IsPresent
summary: Asks the cache service whether the requested icon is already present, returning the service's answer as an int.
evidence: The caller Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry and the callee maybe_Svc_Cecd_QueryRawFile are the only neighbours; the body has no readable evidence section, so whether the predicate tests presence or another service state is unproven.

name: Ui_IconCache_ReadEntryTable
summary: Reads the small index block (service command 0x05): asks for its size, allocates 800 bytes, verifies the 0x6767 magic and the declared count, converts the 8-byte entries into pointers at +0x159 and returns the number of entries.
evidence: Its four callers are the icon-cache cluster (Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry, Ui_IconCache_Open, Ui_IconCache_Create, Ui_IconCache_SetPage), which pins the service even though those caller names are themselves still low-confidence; the 0x6767 magic and the (size-8)>>3 count check in the body are exactly an entry-table reader.

name: maybe_Font_GlyphCache_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a cache object: releases the page array at +0x648, destroys each 0x20-byte page, then releases the three handles and the shared base.
evidence: Confident callees std_destroy_range, Pack_Handle_Dtor, Pack_ReleaseHandle and Gfx_SceneSprite_Release pin it as a destructor of a resource-owning cache, but nothing in the body or the neighbours mentions glyphs or fonts, so that part of the name is still a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_StatusParamWindow_DtorB
signature: void maybe_Ui_StatusParamWindow_DtorB(void *self, u32 arg2, int arg3)
summary: Damaged-decompile variant of the status window destructor: same vtable and child cleanup, but the object pointer is reconstructed from a shifted argument, so only the class identity is certain.
evidence: It still uses the g_003F2944 vtable plus Ui_Object_DtorBase and Ui_LayoutRef_Release, and its body is identical to 0x003F2904; the base pointer is lost (arg3>>9>>8), so nothing beyond the destructor role can be asserted.

name: maybe_Anim2D_SpriteNodeDtorC
summary: Destructor of a sprite node that also destroys its embedded 8-entry range: installs the two base vtables, runs the array destructor on the 0x48-byte block at +0x298, unlinks the node and frees it.
evidence: std_destroy_range and Field_Object_DtorBase are confident, and the two vtable literals 0x75D888/0x75D55C identify the class as a 2D actor/sprite node, but the Anim2D/SpriteNode wording is still inferred from the vtables rather than from a named sibling.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a UI widget: installs the two base-class vtables, destroys the array of eight-byte sub-objects at +0x298, unlinks the widget's intrusive list nodes and frees the object.
evidence: std_destroy_range and Field_Object_DtorBase are confident and the vtable/linked-list pattern is clear, but the class is only identified as some UI object - the Widget wording comes from the shared base, not from a named sibling.

name: maybe_Script_SqValueList_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the Squirrel-value array holder: restores the base vtable, unlinks itself from its owner's child list, releases the refcounted block at +0x1C, destroys every 8-byte element through the SQObjectPtr destructor and installs the base-class vtable.
evidence: The refcount release at +4 of the object at +0x1C and the per-element destructor 0x001BF798 (the header identifies it as SQObjectPtr::~SQObjectPtr by its refcount test) point at a Squirrel-value array, and std_destroy_range is a confident callee. But the owner/child unlink uses an in_r12 register that Ghidra lost, so the flatter 'SqValueList' name stays unconfirmed and below 0.5.

name: maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_Dtor
summary: Destructor for a character status window: destroys the nine 0x36C-byte character slots that start at +0x13C, installs the base vtable and unlinks the window lists.
evidence: std_destroy_range is confident and the nine 0x36C slots at +0x13C are visible, but the status-window class name comes only from the guessed prefix - no named sibling in the cluster confirms the owner.

name: maybe_Ui_MenuInstance_DtorEmbeddedArrays
summary: Tears down a menu/manager instance: stores the passed vtable, destroys the 16-element array of 0xE4-byte panes at +0xC8, destroys the 16-element 0x58-byte array inside the shared sub-object, re-registers it and finally frees it.
evidence: std_destroy_range is confident and the two 16-element array destructors are explicit, but the only other neighbour is a maybe_ battle-effect dtor, so the menu-instance identity of the object is still unproven.

name: Ui_Window_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor of a large window object: clears the member at +0x1E4, releases the reference-counted block at +0x1E8, frees the five 0x50-byte panes at +0x30 and destroys the embedded intrusive list node.
evidence: The caller is the confident Ui_HopeSelect_FreeResources, and the callees std_destroy_range, Pack_ReleaseHandle, Pack_FreeHandleEntry and Ui_Object_DtorBase are all confident, which pins it as the window base destructor; vtable 0x0075F7F8 is installed as slot 0.

name: maybe_Ui_JockeyPanel_HandleInput
summary: Per-frame input handler: reacts to confirm/cancel, plays the error sound 0xEC0 when the selection is invalid and drives the panel state machine (7 = accept, 8 = back).
evidence: Confident callees Menu_Cursor_HasTarget, Snd_RequestBgmPlay and Sound_PlaySeById confirm the input-handling role, but the JockeyPanel class name is unbacked - the function has no caller and the vtable 0x00301AB4 has no named sibling.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_CtorB
signature: void maybe_Ui_DiveForm_CtorB(u32 object, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Second constructor variant of the dive-form window hierarchy: calls the confident Ui_DiveForm_Ctor, initialises the member pair and constructs the state-sequence array; the B suffix only distinguishes it from 0x003096D4.
evidence: Ui_DiveForm_Ctor and Ui_Object_InitMemberPair are confident callees and vtable 0x0075ABC4 belongs to the same family, but the two ctor variants have identical call shapes, so which one belongs to which derived class is unresolved.

name: Model_AttachAccessoryMesh
summary: Creates the accessory mesh (named meshAcc) for a character model and attaches it: builds the mesh object, applies the layout config, spawns its effect, attaches it to the Head node and increments the model's child count.
evidence: The string literal meshAcc is resolved by the function itself, and the callees Gfx_MeshObject_Init, Model_AttachSlot_Setup, Model_Attach_SpawnEffect and Item_LookupRecord are all confident; the sibling 0x003823EC uses the same meshAcc lookup together with the R_Weapon/Head node names.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_ProcessGuardCommand
summary: Command branch of the battle action sequence: when the actor has no ready action it sets state 0x76 on it, otherwise it queues command 0x4B for the actor.
evidence: The caller Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchCommand is confident, but the callees are the balloon/popup helpers (Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor, Ui_PopupEntry_PlayById) and nothing in the body mentions guarding - the Guard wording is still inherited from the first pass.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_ProcessStatusCommand
summary: Handles the status-effect command: if the actor carries one of the effect ids 0xD/0xE/0xF it clears them, otherwise it queues command 0x4B for the actor.
evidence: The caller Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchCommand is confident and the 0xD/0xE/0xF effect-id tests are visible, but the callees are the balloon/popup helpers and the command it queues is the same 0x4B as the sibling, so which game command this is remains a guess.

name: Text_BuildMessageGlyphRun
summary: Builds the glyph run for a message: looks up the message record, allocates/caches the glyph table sized to the next power of two, selects the message box's sprite span and copies the line; returns the message id.
evidence: The callees are now the confident Text_CopyMessageLine, Text_GetRecordString, Ui_SpriteSpan_Select and Ui_TextFormat_ReleaseSlot, and the message-record lookup plus the pow2 table allocation are visible - the glyph-run reading is supported.

name: maybe_Field_EntrySet_Populate
summary: Fills an entry set from the field tables: every id of the table at world+0x24A98 becomes a 0xE1 entry, and every one of the 90 slots whose type byte equals 7 becomes a 0xE5 entry.
evidence: The caller Ui_NotifyList_Ctor and the callees Mem_AllocAligned_2, std_ConstructArray and std_List_MergeSort give the list-container shape, but Field and EntrySet come only from the first pass and the 0xE1/0xE5 entry kinds are still unexplained constants.

name: Ui_CameraAnimWindow_Init
summary: Initialiser for the window that previews camera animations: resolves the resource id of the passed entry to its name, copies it into the 32-byte name field at +0x370 and sets three visible rows.
evidence: The cmtsa camera-animation string belongs to the same class (sibling 0x003EDD10 formats %s_loop.cmtsa into the same +0x370 field), and the Ui_ListWindow_SetRowsPerPage idiom of 3 rows matches the body; the vtable slot +0x34 is where the class initialises from a record.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SetTableIndexFromId
summary: Initialiser that resolves a resource id to its slot index in the window's lookup table and stores it as a byte at +0x220 after the base sub-object is created.
evidence: The base initialiser 0x005F541C and the lazy 0x10-byte-entry table idiom are shared with the camera-anim window, but the loop bound 12 and the byte at +0x220 have no named consumer, so which window class this is stays open.

name: maybe_Os_CriticalSectionObject_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a small engine object that owns a lock: installs the class vtable, runs the two base cleanups, and if the lock word is set performs the kernel lock-release software interrupt and clears it.
evidence: The callers now include the confident Ui_TitleScreen_Dtor, Fs_Worker_Dtor and Gfx_StreamSlot_Shutdown, and the callees Gfx_CommandBuffer_Release and Os_InitEventFlag are confident, so it is a reusable teardown of an object with a kernel lock; the software interrupt number's exact meaning is still unverified.

name: BattleScene_RefreshCommandWidgets
summary: Refreshes the battle command widgets: for every visible list item it enables/disables the widget's sub-elements, commits the equipment node changes of the displayed model and lays the units out again.
evidence: The callees are now the confident Model_Equip_CommitNodeChanges, Ui_GlyphSlot_Reset, Ui_Widget_CountChildren and Container_List_CountVisible, and the body calls the layout pass at the end - the command-widget refresh reading is supported.

name: Ui_Part_MatchAnimRecord
summary: Tests whether an animation record applies to this part: it walks the global 0x20-byte record table, matches the part slot id and the four condition lists (byte, byte, u16 and u16-list) and finally checks the record's two trailing condition ids against the current work flags.
evidence: The callers are now the confident Ui_Part_SetupFromAnimRecord, Ui_Part_SetupAttachFromRecord, Ui_MessagePage_Build and Ui_BagCategory_CountItems, all of which use it as the per-part record predicate; the 0x20-byte record stride and the four condition searches are visible in the body.

name: Gfx_WaitSyncSubmit
signature: int Gfx_WaitSyncSubmit(u32 arg1, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Waits for the graphics/display state machine to leave its transient states and submits a command, retrying on the busy result codes with a 10-tick sleep; returns the submit result.
evidence: The callers Engine_Initialize and Engine_ShutdownAllSubsystems are confident, and the callees now include the confident Svc_SendRequest2/Svc_SendRequestByte plus Os_UnlockScheduler, which matches a submit-with-wait helper used during engine bring-up and teardown.

name: maybe_Gfx_WaitSyncSubmitNoLock
signature: int maybe_Gfx_WaitSyncSubmitNoLock(u32 arg1, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Lock-free copy of the 0x107D00 wait-and-submit sequence: it performs the same gate/spin/submit calls without the lock helpers.
evidence: The callee set is the same three confident service calls as 0x107D00 minus the gates, but nothing calls it directly in the readable C, so both the no-lock and the Gfx wording rest on the comparison with its neighbour.

name: maybe_Os_SetSyncState
summary: Atomically replaces a synchronisation object's state word with -1 (mode 0) or -2 (mode != 0) and returns the previous state, forcing a wake-up/failure state on a thread or event object.
evidence: Sixteen callers spread over unrelated engine modules (Gfx_OpenGpuChannel, Ui_PresentWindow_Ctor, Ui_IconCache_WorkerThread, sound and filesystem init) confirm it is a generic OS helper, but the meaning of the -1/-2 states is still not recoverable.

name: maybe_Os_PerfSample_Loop
summary: One sampling pass of the SDK timing/profiling loop: for each configured entry it starts the counter, sleeps and accumulates elapsed microseconds, stopping early at the 0x3FE marker, then sets the state word to 3 or 0.
evidence: The caller Gfx_OpenGpuChannel and the callees (timer read/convert helpers) are the only named neighbours and they do not mention profiling; the 1000000 microsecond constant and the 0x7B0080 table are the only support for the sampling reading.

name: maybe_Script_ReadArg1Number
summary: Not a real entry point: an inlined read-argument-1-as-a-number fragment of the Squirrel native at 0x0014872C (Script_Native_TokenizeString). It reads argument slot 1, accepts the 0x4000003 float tag and converts it to int.
evidence: The first instruction is bl 0x5B5C6C (sq_getstackobj) with index vm+0x34+1, and the enclosing ARM prologue is at 0x0014872C, which is now the confident Script_Native_TokenizeString; so the behaviour description is right but the address is not a callable function, hence the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Script_ReadArg2Number
summary: Not a real entry point: the inlined read-argument-2-as-a-number fragment of the same Squirrel native at 0x0014872C, identical to 0x00148780 but with index vm+0x34+2.
evidence: Same bl 0x5B5C6C (sq_getstackobj) and 0x4000003 float-tag handling as 0x00148780, inside the now confidently named Script_Native_TokenizeString; the chunk has no prologue of its own.

name: Field_Gimmick_SpawnAnchorEffects
summary: Rebuilds the gimmick's anchors and spawns one effect instance at each anchor, storing the two handles at +0x10C/+0x110, then plays the descriptor sound effects at +0xB0/+0xB2.
evidence: The callees Field_Path_GetPosition, Field_Path_GetTangent, Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and Sound_PlaySeById are confident, and the body builds the anchor matrix from the path tangent before creating the instance - the anchor-effect reading is supported.

name: Field_Gimmick_ApplyConfigBlock
summary: Copies the gimmick's pending configuration block (+0x18..+0x30) into the active block (+0x54..+0x6C), applies it to the actor group and then runs the layout update 0x5E0FA0.
evidence: The body's field-to-field copies are explicit and the callees now include the confident Snd_CommitPendingBgmId and Sound_PlaySeById; the only consumer of the applied block is the layout update, which this function calls.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_RowPanel_BuildRows
summary: Builds the member status/message rows of a party status window: per member it composes the name-plus-value row and spawns the row's popup entries.
evidence: The only caller is the window's own update (maybe_Battle_Ui_RowPanel_Update) and the callees are the generic popup/effect/sound helpers; no pane name or row constant confirms the Battle/Rows wording.

name: Field_Gimmick_SpawnVariantEffect
signature: int Field_Gimmick_SpawnVariantEffect(void *self, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Gimmick reaction dispatcher: switches on the descriptor variant id at +0xB4 (0..5) to pick an effect id, a sound id and a part count, resolves the actor and spawns the matching effect instance.
evidence: The switch on +0xB4 with the visible case groups (effect ids 2/5/1/0xC/8, SE ids 3/6/10/12) plus the confident Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and Sound_PlaySeById calls support the variant-dispatch reading; it is vtable slot 5 of the gimmick base (0x783F14).

name: Field_Gimmick_SpawnNutEffect
summary: Spawns the named field effect Bt_Nut anchored to the placed party member: builds the placement record (member id, direction, scale) from +0x18 and the actor group, creates the effect and plays its sound.
evidence: The function itself references the string literal Bt_Nut, and the callees Field_ActorGroup_PlaceMember and Field_Actor_UpdateAttachment are confident; the placement record is filled from +0x18 before the create call.

name: Field_Gimmick_ConfigureFromAssetList
summary: Configures a gimmick from a short list of asset ids: resolves each 4-byte entry through the asset table, stores the resulting ids and mode bytes at +0xD0..+0xD8, marks every actor-group member with +0x288 = 1, builds the group placement descriptor, plays the sound and finally pushes a 12-byte component description to the field component.
evidence: The body resolves each entry through func_0063E54C and applies the group descriptor through the confident Field_ActorGroup_ApplyFormation; the component push uses the same 0x3D5648 idiom as the neighbouring gimmick functions, and the old draft name SetupBossParts invented a boss that is not in the code.

name: Field_Gimmick_PlayScreenReactionB
summary: Second screen-reaction variant: when the sub-state at +0x54 is 6 it builds the reaction record, hands it to the UI effect hook, updates the part state and stops the BGM when the reaction ends.
evidence: The f_54 == 6 guard, the confident Snd_RequestBgmStop callee and the same UI-core component path as the named reaction siblings support the reading; only the B suffix is arbitrary disambiguation.

name: Ui_SceneWindow_Open
summary: Opens a menu window that owns 3D scene sprites: releases the previous scene objects, hides the sprite-layer flag, copies each child's +0x9C value into the window list and plays window SE 0xD3. Its close counterpart is the next vtable slot.
evidence: The scene-object release (maybe_Ui_CollectObjectsByMask) and Sound_PlaySeById are the only callees, and the next vtable entry 0x004FB70C is the matching close on the same list at +0x2C; the GUI-side role is consistent with both.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_PartyPanel_PlaySe
summary: Plays the window's confirmation sound and spawns the associated popup entry for the current row.
evidence: The caller is the panel's own update and the callees are Sound_PlaySeById, Sound_GetPlayer and Os_GetGameWork; the name says little and no pane/row id confirms the PartyPanel wording, so it stays maybe_.

name: Field_Gimmick_ClosePanelAndPlaySe
summary: Closes the gimmick's UI panel through the panel handle from the UI core and plays sound effect g_005D5A18.
evidence: The body is Ui_GetCore -> UI component -> panel close call plus Sound_PlaySeById(g_005D5A18); the panel helper itself is still a maybe_ name, so the operation is clear but the helper identity is not.

name: Field_Gimmick_LayoutPartsForAction
summary: Lays out and tints the parts of an animated gimmick: per part it computes the local offset relative to the actor, sets the part matrix and tint span, and builds the part's action label using the string Run.
evidence: The Run string literal, the confident Field_Gimmick_GetRandomPartOffset callee and the per-part matrix/tint writes support the reading; the only open point is the exact action name the label is built for.

name: Field_Gimmick_SpawnEffectB
signature: int Field_Gimmick_SpawnEffectB(void *self, int arg2, int arg3)
summary: Second effect-spawn variant of the gimmick base: builds the spawn transform from the actor matrix plus the descriptor offset (+0x98/+0xF4), creates the effect instance and applies the colour record and sound.
evidence: The body mirrors the named variant 0x005D3D8C but reads the descriptor offsets from f_A8, and the confident Effect_FindOrCreateInstance / Sound_PlaySeById calls plus vtable 0x783F80 place it in the same spawn family.

name: Field_Gimmick_BuildPartSlots
summary: Clears the eight 0xC-byte part slots and fills them with the handles of parts 0..partCount-1 of the actor, storing each handle with its repeat count and a constant 3, then plays the slot sound.
evidence: The 8-iteration loop writing {handle, count, 3} into +0x14+i*0xC is visible, and the callees now include the confident Sound_PlaySeById; the part handles come from the actor (0x650D34) rather than from a named slot helper, which is why the name stays descriptive.

name: Field_Gimmick_PlayScreenReaction
summary: Plays the screen-space reaction of a gimmick: takes the actor, builds the reaction matrix, hands it to the UI effect hook, applies it to the actor and plays sound g_005D7E14.
evidence: Both the UI-core component path and Sound_PlaySeById(g_005D7E14) are visible, and the sibling 0x005DE300/0x005DF29C share the same component call; the matrix construction is the only inferred part.

name: Field_Gimmick_PrepareUiReaction
summary: Prepares the screen reaction of a gimmick: when the flag at +0x1BC is 1 it resolves the referenced part, builds the reaction record from the part's colour at +0x224 and hands it to the UI effect hook, then plays the sound.
evidence: The f_1BC == 1 guard and the record built from part+0x224 are visible, and the UI-core component call plus Sound_PlaySeById are the same pair the sibling PlayScreenReaction uses.

name: Field_Gimmick_PlayVariantReaction
summary: Plays the reaction for one of the gimmick's variants: switches on rec->f_10->f_10 (0..5) to pick the sound and the part counts, applies it to the actor and plays the sound.
evidence: The switch on the record's variant field with the visible case assignments and the confident Sound_PlaySeById call support the name; the only caller is the still-unnamed 0x005DFA3C group.

name: Field_Gimmick_InitSlotIds
summary: Distributes fresh ids to the eight per-slot entries at +0x1C (each from the generic id counter), stores the group-dependent value at +0x3C and plays the sound.
evidence: The 8-iteration loop writing id+1 into +0x1C+i*4 and the assignment from the group table at g_005E2268 are visible; the counter helper 0x0051B1FC is still low-confidence but the loop semantics are clear.

name: maybe_Actor_PlayTableAction
summary: Looks up the actor's animation/action record in the table at ctx+0x3E4 (0xC-byte entries indexed by f_160->f_120) and plays its sound/action, using the byte at record+4 as the action id.
evidence: The table walk and the play call are visible, but the callees are Game_GetDataManager, Sound_GetPlayer and the maybe_ sound-from-table helper, and there are no callers - the Actor prefix is still a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_OpenWindowForFieldState
summary: Opens/configures a UI window from the current field state: reads the overlay state byte at +0x281, resolves the window record through the 0x63D6B8 table and calls the window setup with the derived parameters.
evidence: The field-state byte (+0x281) and the record lookup are visible, but the setup helper is still the low-confidence sound/table helper and there are no callers; both halves of the name remain inferred.

name: maybe_Sound_FadeTimer_Get
summary: Returns the BGM fade time window: while a fade is pending it starts the pending fade and returns the short window, otherwise the default window from the same global table.
evidence: The body only selects between two pairs of globals under a pending-fade flag and calls the sound helper; with no callers and only Sound_GetPlayer/Ui_GetCore as named callees, the fade-timer reading is unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_Shop_StopFadeAndSound
summary: Shop-window helper that stops the pending fade and the associated sound through the UI core and sound player.
evidence: Recovered without an evidence header; the only named callees are Sound_GetPlayer and Ui_GetCore, and no caller or vtable slot was found, so the Shop wording is inherited and unverified.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_RowTransition_Tail
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_Ui_RowTransition_Tail(u32 arg1, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Thumb fragment at the end of a state-handler block: walks the 0x12-byte row records, compares word 0 and word 6 and updates the message object at +0x260/+0x7A4; likely the tail of 0x483870 rather than a function of its own.
evidence: Thumb mode while its neighbours are ARM and the absence of a prologue say the boundary is wrong; the 0x12-byte stride matches the row records of 0x483870, but the entry point itself is not trustworthy.

name: maybe_Battle_PartyMember_UpdateEnter
summary: Entry-state handler for a party-member display object: posts the appear effect/sound and advances once the state counter (0x172/0x17D) elapses.
evidence: The vtable 0x774700 slot 2 and the 0x172/0x17D counters are visible, and Sound_PlaySeById is confident, but the other helpers (state flags, popup spawn, wait timer) are all maybe_ names, so the Enter wording is an inference.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_PlayFrameSounds
summary: Frame-driven sound/state player: plays SE 0xE5F at frame 5 and 0xE60 at frame 25, runs the 0x4A43CC callback at frame 35 and finally advances the stored vtable/handle pair after frame 44.
evidence: The frame comparisons and the two sound ids are explicit, but only Sound_PlaySeById/Sound_GetPlayer are named among the callees and there are no callers; Overlay is still a guess from the 0x72A79C data block.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdateSlotMessages
summary: Per-frame update of the member slots: when the countdown at +0xF8 expires it looks each slot's actor up, injects the action/message id into that actor and plays the slot sound. Vtable slot 20 of the gimmick base.
evidence: The loop over +0xF4 slots at stride 0xC and the handle-table validation of f_94 are visible, and the actor injection goes through the named 0x5E74A0; only the message/sound ids are unnamed constants.

name: Field_Gimmick_UpdateEffectLink
summary: Updates the two-point effect link (beam/rope) of a gimmick: computes both attachment points from the actor matrix and the descriptor offsets, normalises the direction, feeds it to the link-segment update and plays the two descriptor sounds.
evidence: The two endpoint computations plus the confident Sound_PlaySeById calls with f_A8->f_B0/f_B2 are visible, and the link update helper (0x5AFCE8) is shared with the named gimmick effect code; the link-segment helper is still a maybe_ name.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdateReactionC
summary: Third reaction variant: plays a sound for states 8 and 0x10 and applies a 4-step transform on state 0x1A, always returning 1.
evidence: The switch on +0x38 (8/0x10/0x1A) and one Sound_PlaySeById are all the body contains, and 0x006D334C is unnamed; the C suffix and the UpdateReaction family are convention, not evidence.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlayReactionThunk
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_PlayReactionThunk(void *self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: 36-byte Thumb callback that builds the reaction matrix from the part's +0x224, triggers the UI effect hook and plays sound id 300.
evidence: The fragment is only three calls long and two of them (the matrix build and the UI hook) are still maybe_ names, so the thunk role is visible but the reaction wording is not confirmed.

name: Field_Gimmick_RequestSceneBgm
summary: Chooses the scene BGM by area/scene id (f_C->f_1D78): ids 1-3 map to 0x33, 4-6 to 0x3B, 7-8 to 0x36 and 9+ to 0x37, then requests it with Snd_RequestBgmPlay.
evidence: The switch with those exact case groups is visible and the callee Snd_RequestBgmPlay is confident; its twin 0x005DCEC8 repeats the same switch for the stop path.

name: Ui_Panel_PlayBgmAndShow
summary: Requests BGM id 0x11, computes the panel's screen offset relative to the menu state's anchor and recreates the panel at that position.
evidence: The confident Snd_RequestBgmPlay call with id 0x11 and the panel recreation through 0x00213DAC (offset computed from panel+8/+0xC minus the state anchor) are both visible.

name: maybe_Ui_SetFloatParam
summary: Small helper that fetches the UI singleton and forwards the converted float value plus the first argument to 0x001ED7CC.
evidence: The only named callee is Sound_GetPlayer and the target 0x001ED7CC is unnamed, so neither the UI nor the float-parameter wording could be checked against a named consumer.

name: maybe_Ui_CloseWindowOfType
summary: Closes a UI window when it is an instance of the class whose vtable is g_0015B1A0: walks the class chain and calls the close helper with 0 on a match.
evidence: The class-chain comparison against g_0015B1A0 is explicit, but the close helper is still a maybe_ name and there are no callers, so the close-window reading is inferred rather than confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_CloseWindowOfType2
summary: Variant of 0x0015B118 for a different window class (vtable g_0015F1F8): walks the class chain and closes the matching window through the same close helper.
evidence: The body is identical in shape to 0x0015B118 and differs only in the vtable constant, but both functions rest on the same still-unnamed close helper and neither has a caller.

name: Ui_Window_AdvanceCmd0F
summary: Polls the animation handle stored by Ui_Window_SetResultAnimation; once the animation has finished (and the window is not in a special state) it clears the handle and advances the frame script to command 0x0F.
evidence: The handle poll (0x63071C) and the script advance (vtable +0x14 with 0x0F, then +0x10) are explicit, and the function pairs with 0x00262E30 which creates that handle; the 0x0F command id is what the name records.

name: maybe_Ui_Cue_Finish
summary: Ends a UI cue object when its sound has finished: asks the sound system whether the handle at +0x10 is still active, then clears the handle and reloads the descriptor's callback words (+0x78/+0x7C).
evidence: The handle test and the HYD-descriptor callback pair are visible, but the handle helper is only maybe_Svc_Handle_IsStale and there are no callers, so both the Cue and the Finish wording stay inferred.

name: maybe_Ui_Cue_ResetIfIdle
summary: If the sound system reports an idle/quiet slot (bit 28 of the manager word at +4) the cue resets itself to the neutral callback pair and clears its timer state.
evidence: The bit-28 test and the callback pair from the same HYD descriptor are visible, but only Sound_GetPlayer is a named callee and the object's identity as a cue is a convention of the neighbouring maybe_ names.

name: maybe_Ui_Cue_Start
signature: int maybe_Ui_Cue_Start(void *cue, u16 cueId, int fadeVehicle)
summary: Starts a cue on an idle cue object: records the 16-bit cue id, the three packed parameters and the flag byte, triggers the start or stop callback depending on that flag and copies the initial callback pair; returns 1 when it started and 0 when the object was busy.
evidence: Eight callers in party-panel and special-move UI use it, and the cue-id write plus the two callback calls are visible, but every caller is itself a maybe_ name, so the Cue wording is not confirmed by a confident consumer.

name: maybe_Ui_Event_WaitSoundThenAdvanceA
signature: int maybe_Ui_Event_WaitSoundThenAdvanceA(void *self, int arg2, int b, void *ctxOut)
summary: Event-window state step that waits for a sound handle to finish and then advances the event; the context result is written through ctxOut.
evidence: Recovered without an evidence header; the callees are a maybe_ event-callback dispatcher and a maybe_ save-notify helper, so neither the WaitSound nor the Advance wording could be verified.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_WaitSoundThenAdvanceA
signature: int maybe_Ui_Window_WaitSoundThenAdvanceA(void *self, int arg2, int b, void *ctxOut)
summary: Window state step that waits for a sound handle to finish and then advances the window script.
evidence: Recovered without an evidence header; it has the same callee pair as 0x002857D0 (event-callback dispatcher, save-notify helper) and no confident caller, so the name is still a family guess.

name: maybe_Battle_UiFlow_IsRowActorSelected
summary: Returns self when the row's stored actor/slot id (f_1B4->f_78) is accepted by 0x63071C, otherwise 0; used as a predicate in the battle UI flow table.
evidence: The body is one handle-acceptance query on f_1B4->f_78 and the function is an entry in the flow table 0x00726F90; there is no caller and no confident neighbour, so both Battle_UiFlow and IsSelected remain inferred.

name: maybe_Battle_UiFlow_PlaySeForState
summary: Plays the sound associated with the current flow state: reads the state value at +0x1A8, converts it and forwards it to the sound start through the UI singleton.
evidence: The body is a three-line conversion plus one sound call and the function is a table entry (0x00727078); the state being a flow state is an inference, not a named fact.

name: maybe_Battle_UiFlow_IsEntryUsable
summary: Returns 0 when the entry's stored kind (at +0x58, or +0x64 when flag bit 2 is set) is out of range (>= 0x9E or 0xFF), otherwise keeps the value after asking the acceptance helper.
evidence: The range checks and the flag-bit choice between +0x58 and +0x64 are visible, but the acceptance helper 0x6305F0 is unnamed and the function has no caller, so neither the Entry nor the Usable wording is confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeInfo_TickCraft
summary: Polls the craft action (sound/animation id at +0x224) and, when it finishes, triggers the part's done callback through the script object at +0x11C.
evidence: The handle poll on +0x224 and the script advance (7 then +0x10) are visible, but the only named callee is Sound_GetPlayer and the RecipeInfo class comes purely from the first pass.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeInfo_TickCraftB
summary: Second copy of the craft-finished poll for the alternate recipe slot: same handle poll on +0x224, same script advance.
evidence: Identical body to 0x00450550 (same three calls, same +0x224 handle), so it is a template copy for the second recipe slot; the class name is still unverified.

name: maybe_Ui_TalkWindow_PushEvent
summary: Forwards a queued event to the talk window's input handler through the script/scene context handle.
evidence: The 36-byte body fetches the UI singleton, checks the context pointer and calls the single event-dispatch helper; with no caller and only Sound_GetPlayer named, neither TalkWindow nor PushEvent is verified.

name: maybe_Ui_TalkWindow_CanHandleEvent
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_TalkWindow_CanHandleEvent(void *self, u32 unusedA, u32 unusedB, u32 context)
summary: Checks whether the talk window may consume the next event: returns 1 and pushes event 0x0C to its input handler unless the scene-context flag bit 3 is set.
evidence: The context bit-3 test and the event-0x0C push (virtual +0x14 then +0x10 on self+0x11C) are visible, but the window class is not confirmed by any named neighbour, so it stays maybe_.

name: Field_Gimmick_RequestSceneBgmStop
summary: Same scene-id to BGM-id mapping as 0x005DCE00 (1-3 -> 0x33, 4-6 -> 0x3B, 7-8 -> 0x36, 9+ -> 0x37) but stops that BGM instead of playing it.
evidence: The switch on f_C->f_1D78 is an exact copy of the request path, and this variant calls the stop helper 0x005DCF44 plus the UI singleton; the pair request/stop is what the names describe.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_ActivateActorsInRange
summary: Scans the actor handle range starting at f_C+0x1FDC and enables the state flag at +0x1D3 on each actor of the wanted class, then triggers the follow-up action.
evidence: The handle-table walk with the -1/+2 step and the +0x1D3 flag write are visible, but the walker 0x0066892C and the follow-up 0x005DF11C are unnamed and the function has no caller.

name: maybe_Text_FormatBuildSegments
summary: Builds the linked list of format segments used by the formatter: allocates 0x48-byte nodes, initialises them from the 24-byte spec triples, copies the literal and links them before the parser at 0x0014F93C runs.
evidence: The node size, the +0x0C/+0x10/+0x18 links and the std_Format_ParseSpec callee are explicit, and the caller is the confident Script_Vm_RegisterDefaultDelegates; but the cluster is Squirrel string formatting (Sq_HashTable_*, Script_ObjectPtr_Assign), so whether this belongs to Text or to the script formatter is still open.

name: maybe_Party_BuildStatusSnapshot
summary: Rebuilds a per-party-member snapshot array (one 0x1C-byte entry each) from the live party records, growing the array once when a new member appears.
evidence: The confident callees Party_CountAliveMembers, Party_GetActiveMemberDataByIndex and std_ConstructArray name the source data, but Snapshot is only a description of the copy loop - no consumer of the array was found.

name: Ui_UpdateInput
summary: Per-frame UI input update: picks the active window by type mask, runs the touch/pointer hit test, updates the focused window and refreshes the cursor/selection state.
evidence: The callers are the confident Ui_SceneFlow_Update, and the callees now include Ui_HitTestRows plus Ui_ObjectList_Begin/End, which is exactly the per-frame input sweep the name describes; the 1800-byte body walks the window list and compares the +0x128 sub-type.

name: maybe_Camera_TryStartWork
summary: Starts a queued camera work item when the current one is idle and the work table entry is set: resolves the game context (work+0x54 -> +0x1C) and runs the two camera work helpers.
evidence: The idle gate (owner+0x3C == 0 and the flag byte at +0x11) is visible, but the callees Gfx_ScreenView_ResetAll and the two work helpers do not mention a camera and the caller is the generic scene-flow update, so the Camera wording is still inferred.

name: Gfx_Effect2D_UpdateInstances
signature: void Gfx_Effect2D_UpdateInstances(void *self, int arg2, int arg3, int owner)
summary: Per-frame update of the active 2D effects: advances each instance's animation, applies the current screen/camera offset, removes finished instances and re-links the list.
evidence: The caller is the confident Ui_SceneFlow_Update, the finished-node removal goes through std_RbTree_EraseNode, and the animation/camera-offset helpers operate on uiCore+0x78; the instance list at +0x20/+0x28 is walked and re-linked in the body.

name: maybe_Gfx_UpdateScreenEntries
summary: Per-frame update of the per-screen view entries: walks the two screen blocks (+0x54 and +0xB10), updates each entry's transform and copies the resulting basis vectors.
evidence: The two 0xABC-apart blocks and the float transform mix are visible, but the only named callee is Os_GetGameWork and the caller is the generic scene-flow update; the per-screen reading comes from the block layout, not from a named consumer.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateSmoothFollow
summary: Updates a smoothed follow/interpolation component with up to three targets: picks the active slot, copies its value into the previous/current pair, integrates the per-frame delta into the accumulated x/y offsets and publishes them to the two shared state records.
evidence: The three controller slots at +0xC and the (f_50-f_40)/(f_54-f_44) integration are certain, but the callers are the actor trail actions (Actor_Action_Trail_Start/InitSamples) and the generic scene-flow update, so the Camera reading is still a guess.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_ApplyFade
summary: Runs the scene-flow update and then applies the pending fade/screen effect through the fade routine on self->f_84; returns 1 to keep the state active.
evidence: The body is exactly Ui_SceneFlow_Update followed by the fade-apply call on f_84, and the confident callee pins the first half; the fade routine itself is still unnamed, which is why the confidence stays moderate.

name: maybe_Menu_TeardownWindow
summary: Tears the menu window down: resets the two layout objects, releases the window object, the five slot records and the selection objects, then updates the selection window.
evidence: The caller is the confident Ui_SceneFlow_Update and the five-iteration slot release is visible, but every cleanup helper it calls is still a maybe_ name, so the Menu_TeardownWindow wording is not confirmed.

name: maybe_Casino_SlotMachine_InitSubParts
summary: In-place initialises the three sub-parts of a slot-machine display object: the panel object at +0x5C, the reel/table object at +0x70 and returns the address of the third part at +0xB8.
evidence: The confident caller Ui_SceneFlow_Update and the neighbour 0x3DACB0 (the slot-table update) place it in the slot-machine cluster, but the two constructors it calls are still unnamed, so the SlotMachine wording rests on that neighbourhood.

name: Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry
signature: void Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry(void *self, void *widget, int eventId, u32 stored, int slot, u8 mode)
summary: Appends one entry to the battle command queue: stores the argument in the frame header, copies the widget into the frame slot, writes the event id and the mode byte and advances the frame index when slot 0 is used.
evidence: The callers are the confident battle action producers (Battle_Update, Battle_ExecuteItemAction, Battle_QueueAbilityAction, Battle_SelectAiActions), and the writes into the per-frame slot block plus the frame-index increment are visible - this is the battle command queue, not a UI queue as the old name said.

name: maybe_Ui_GetScaledValue
summary: Shared helper: converts the key through 0x48F08C, resets the animation slot at work+0x5C+0x4218 and returns the value scaled by the float at 0x001681FC.
evidence: The calls and the scaling constant are visible, but the callee side is a maybe_ stat-bar helper and the callers are the battle queue functions, so the Ui_ prefix and the purpose of the key are both unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_ValidateTarget
summary: Validates whether a target unit can be targeted: checks the target's alive predicate, compares the party/group ids and verifies the targeting eligibility flags.
evidence: The only caller is the confident Battle_SelectAiActions and the only named callee is Game_GetDataManager; the body does compare group ids and call a target predicate, but no named helper confirms the exact eligibility rules.

name: Battle_Start
summary: Virtual battle-start entry: clears the current action slot, initialises the world battle interface, resets the action flags, syncs the unit model transforms, releases the previous battle scene object and calls the manager's vtable +0x2C to finish initialisation.
evidence: The callees Battle_SyncUnitModelTransforms, Menu_ResetSlotRecords, Ui_BalloonPool_Reset and Ui_MessageWindow_ReleaseChildren are all confident and are exactly the per-battle reset set; it has no direct caller because it is reached through the manager vtable.

name: Field_NpcGetActionAnimId
summary: Resolves the animation/action record for the NPC's current action slot and writes its id into out->f_C; when the table index is valid it advances the slot cursor (wrapping over the entry count) and reads the animation id.
evidence: All four callers are the confident NPC action functions (Field_NpcActionRun, Field_NpcActionRunUpdate, Field_NpcAction_MoveToOffset, Field_Npc_FaceTarget), and the slot cursor +0x2A4 with the wrap and the out->f_C write are visible in the body.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_ApplyModelSettings
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_ApplyModelSettings(void *self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Applies a scene object's model settings: sets the model size, refreshes the object handle, resolves the object's actor record by id and stores it at +0x22C, then updates the actor's movement state.
evidence: The confident callees Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize, Field_SceneObject_RefreshModelAndCellVisibility, Field_SceneObject_ResetAnimation and Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation show what the function really does; the old ApplyTransform wording implied transform math that is not in the body, but the caller is itself a maybe_ gimmick name, so the new name keeps the maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_Refresh
summary: Lightweight refresh of a scene object: updates its animation, re-applies the actor movement state derived from +0x246 and calls the follow-up layout step when the flags at +0x29F/+0xB8 are set.
evidence: The only named callee is Field_SceneObject_ResetAnimation and there are no callers; the movement-state re-application (0x5E7848 with 2 or 0) is visible but the Refresh wording is generic.

name: Model_SetupObject
summary: Chooses the model/attachment record from the primary or fallback reference, reads its model id and copies the record's transform and scale onto the object before marking it set up.
evidence: The callers are the confident Field_Npc_InitTalkBalloons and Field_Npc_InitEmoteBalloon, and the callees Math_BuildQuaternionFromEuler and Gfx_Node_SetEulerRotation are confident; the primary/fallback record choice and the transform copy are visible in the body.
